  • Focus on your development by attaining industry recognised certifications.

  • Be available for occasional on-call duties and on-site client engagements, as needed.

  • Certifications: Relevant certifications such as CREST CRT, CREST CCT, OSCP, OSWE, OSCE, or equivalent level.

  • Experience: At least two years in penetration testing, covering network, web, and internal tests and customer engagements.

  • Tools: Proficiency with tools like Burpsuite Pro, Nessus, and other industry standards.

  • Communication: Strong verbal and written skills for stakeholder management, collaboration and report writing.

  • Independence: Ability to work solo or as part of a team on penetration tests.

  • Eligibility: Right to work in the UK and eligibility for security clearance.

Key Attributes

  • Analytical thinker with a proactive, detail-oriented approach.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, capable of engaging with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Ability to work effectively under pressure and adapt to rapidly changing threat landscapes.

  • Commitment to maintaining the highest ethical and professional standards.

jobs.title: Senior Voice Routing Specialist
jobs.description:
The Challenge

We connect over 500’000 callers in 190 countries: that represents 36,000 calling corridors and over 100 million calling minutes. We work with various global suppliers optimising for call quality. It’s complex. Each calling corridor has its own quality quirks and legal and regulatory rules to work within. We want someone to own call quality and routing holistically across all of it: routing daily to optimize what's happening right now, while watching the data for the long-term trends that tell us where to fix things next.

A failed call is not a metric to us. It's someone not hearing their mother's voice or its an important business call that fails. We also have real ambitions to scale calling well beyond where we are today, so this complexity isn't going anywhere. It's only going to grow.

Talk360 has been profitable since 2025, expanding beyond our core calling app into embedded, B2B2C calling for partners. We are lean, around 30 people globally, spread across the Netherlands, South Africa, Nigeria, Suriname, Turkey, Egypt, Kenya, Ukraine, and beyond. That means this role has real scope from day one: no layers between you and the decisions that matter, and no shortage of things worth tackling.

This is a remote opportunity.

What You'll Do

  • Own call quality holistically: hold the full picture of call quality end to end, working with the team on both the daily grind and the long-term view, moving fluidly between quick fixes and structured experiments.

  • Manage zones, codes, and origins: own and continuously refine our zone, dialing code, and call origin management, keeping the underlying structure clean and accurate across all 900 zones.

  • Update routing continuously: change routing several times a day, from immediate fixes to longer-running tests of new suppliers.

  • Work cross-functionally by design: partner daily with Ozcan, who owns supplier account management and deal creation, and Mahmoud, who runs hourly monitoring and support-team escalations to suppliers. Work with Ewan on automating the processes behind routing, and with Product and CRM to improve the experience for our end users.

  • Move routing toward automation: work toward (semi) automated routing and pricing, reducing how much of this still runs on manual, single-person work.


What You'll Bring

  • Hands-on experience with international A-Z calling and telco routing: zones, codes, LCR, and SIP response codes, built at a telco, carrier, or comms platform with real cross-border calling experience.

  • NOC or technical support background: comfortable troubleshooting live voice traffic and reading call detail records and quality metrics like ASR and ACD.

  • Exposure to a routing/testing platform such as iTest or an equivalent tool. Familiarity with Digitalk Cloud Carrier (DCC), our current routing platform, is a plus.

  • Nice to have: working technical literacy in SIP signalling and SBC concepts

Who You Are

  • Process driven and meticulous: you build the audit trail as you go, not after something goes wrong. You are methodical and analytical by nature, and you would rather have a clean, repeatable process than a clever one-off fix.

  • Hands-on: you do the routing work yourself, day to day, not just direct others to do it.

  • A strong communicator: equally at ease explaining a routing issue to Product or Marketing as debating a fix with a supplier's NOC team.

  • Ownership without a script: you see a bottleneck and you fix it rather than wait to be asked.

  • Genuinely commercial: you understand a dropped call or a bad route costs Talk360 real money and a real user's trust, not just an SLA breach.

Recruitment Process

  1. Recruiter screening

  2. Hiring manager screening with COO

  3. Technical interview

  4. Case study

What you get

Learning and growth

  • €1,500 annual personal development budget, plus access to company-wide training sessions to keep learning and evolving. 

Time to recharge 

  • 25 vacation days 

  • Option to swap two public holidays per year for days that better reflect your culture or beliefs 

  • Recharge Fridays, unlocked when team targets are met (we'll tell you more during the interview) 

Work from anywhere

  • As a global and diverse team, we encourage you to work from another city or country for up to 2 weeks per year, gain fresh perspectives and spark new ideas. 

A team you'll actually want to be part of 

  • Weekly team lunch every Thursday 

  • Regular team moments and outings 

  • An international and diverse team, with colleagues from the Netherlands, South Africa, Nigeria, Suriname, Turkey, Egypt, Kenya, Ukraine and beyond

An environment to grow and make impact

  • A collaborative environment where you can learn from others, take ownership, and contribute to a meaningful mission

About Talk360

Talk360 was founded with a clear purpose: to become the most accessible and reliable calling app for African diaspora communities, both within Africa and abroad. For our users, calls are not transactional, they are emotional lifelines to family, friends, and essential support networks. When service quality drops, they feel it immediately. That responsibility drives everything we build.

As we continue to grow, we are expanding beyond our own B2C app. We are now launching our first embedded calling products within partner platforms, bringing Talk360’s technology into new ecosystems and enabling partners to offer international calling directly within their own products.

Our ambition is bold: to become the world’s most trusted way to call any real phone number — connecting migrants, travellers, professionals, and businesses across the globe.

jobs.title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer (Web + Infrastructure)
jobs.description:
Searoutes makes the emissions data that shippers use to run and reduce their
logistics. It is an operational problem before it is an environmental one, and
in our hands it is mostly an engineering one.

We are hiring a senior engineer who works across our web frontend and our
infrastructure — the same two codebases, in the same week. Someone who ships a
product screen on Monday, changes an identity-provider flow on Wednesday, and
considers those the same job.

We are looking for a broad profile rather than a specialist. The next year is
mostly platform work with a user-facing edge — user management, API gateway
management, payments, SEO, and a great deal of compliance, GDPR and ISO 27001.

If you are passionate about the environment, proactive and pragmatic in getting
things done, and love to work in a complex but fascinating industry where you
learn every day — then this is the place for you.

The work in front of us

Some of the items on our tech roadmap for the coming year. Bets are picked a
cycle at a time and shared out, so you would take the ones that suit you and
grow into the rest.

  • Product and marketing UI in React — multi-brand, WCAG AA, strong on
    technical SEO, fast enough to hold a performance budget.
  • User management and identity — Keycloak realms, organisation hierarchies,
    partner brokering, and the entitlement model in the app.
  • API gateway work in APISIX — routes, plugins and auth policy as code.
  • Payments and billing.
  • ISO 27001 and GDPR — access control, change management, audit logging,
    observability and alerting, consent and retention.
  • The infrastructure underneath — Pulumi in TypeScript, Docker Swarm on
    Hetzner, Cloudflare at the edge, Tailscale for all engineer and CI access.
  • Third-party integrations — usually the seam between two systems that were
    never designed to meet.

Nobody arrives fluent in all of that, and we are not expecting it. We want
someone strong across a good part of it, comfortable being new to the rest, and
used to working things out — with a team and with agents, rather than alone.

Also in daily use: Postgres and PostGIS, Valkey, ClickHouse; Vite, Tailwind and
Radix; Jest and Playwright; GitHub Actions; HAProxy. Most of what we write is
TypeScript, strict — though our core API is Java and Spring, and the identity
layer has Java in it too, so how far you go into that side is up to you.

How we work

LLM-native, in the codebases you would work in. They are built around
agent-assisted development rather than merely tolerant of it — the conventions,
the tooling and the review gates all assume it. Agents do most of the
implementation and much of the review; humans design, verify and approve. What
we are really hiring for is judgement over output you did not write by hand:
knowing what to specify, what to check, and what to throw away. The bar did not
move when the tooling did.

Shape Up, and you own what you take. Roughly three weeks of building, then a
week of cooldown, with bets chosen at a betting table. We are small enough that
an area becomes yours quickly — you make the calls inside it and you answer for
how it turns out. We hand out problems, not the steps that solve them.

Remote first, with most of the team in Europe and everyone together in person at
least twice a year. Significant technical decisions get written down, and a
green build is never on its own enough to merge.

Requirements

You'll thrive here if you have…

  • Senior full-stack experience — you have owned features from the browser to
    the machine they run on.
  • A track record of taking something and running with it — a domain, a
    migration, a subsystem you took on, decided and stayed accountable for.
  • Taste. You can tell a good design from a merely plausible one, and you
    will reject work that functions but is not right — your own, and an agent's.
  • React beyond the client — server rendering, static generation, data
    loading and hydration; you know what runs where and why it matters.
  • TypeScript at strict — typed boundaries, and an instinct for when types
    are carrying real weight.
  • Infrastructure as code — Pulumi ideally; Terraform if you are ready to
    pick up Pulumi.
  • Containers and Linux in production — not writing a Dockerfile, but
    debugging a service on a machine you have to SSH into.
  • Postgres beyond queries — backup and restore, migrations, what a schema
    change does under load.
  • Wholehearted LLM-assisted development — you use coding agents daily, have
    opinions about steering them, and review their output as critically as a
    colleague's.
  • Integration instincts — third-party APIs, webhooks, OAuth/OIDC, and
    patience for other people's undocumented edge cases.
  • A working day that overlaps ours: based within CET ±3.
  • Fluent in English, our working language.

Nice to have

  • Identity and API gateways in depth — Keycloak, OIDC, SAML brokering, APISIX.
  • Compliance from the inside — an ISO 27001 certification lived through, or GDPR
    beyond a cookie banner.
  • Payment systems, billing models, or PSP integrations.
  • Observability and alerting — Prometheus, Grafana or equivalent.
  • Experience in the maritime, logistics or freight industry.
  • Familiarity with emissions accounting frameworks (GHG Protocol, GLEC, EU
    ETS..).

Benefits

As part of our team, you will:

  • 🌱 Have a chance to re-shape the future of climate in the logistics.
  • 👩‍💻 Be empowered to deliver your best work remotely, and get a stipend to set
    you up.
  • 🏄‍♂️ Have a flat hierarchy, where you will have direct access to the founders
    and won't be tied up in politics.
  • 🎓 Have a high degree of learning and ownership in a dynamic environment.
  • 🏝 Take part in our team-building events.

jobs.title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer (Web + Infrastructure)
jobs.description:
Searoutes makes the emissions data that shippers use to run and reduce their
logistics. It is an operational problem before it is an environmental one, and
in our hands it is mostly an engineering one.

We are hiring a senior engineer who works across our web frontend and our
infrastructure — the same two codebases, in the same week. Someone who ships a
product screen on Monday, changes an identity-provider flow on Wednesday, and
considers those the same job.

We are looking for a broad profile rather than a specialist. The next year is
mostly platform work with a user-facing edge — user management, API gateway
management, payments, SEO, and a great deal of compliance, GDPR and ISO 27001.

If you are passionate about the environment, proactive and pragmatic in getting
things done, and love to work in a complex but fascinating industry where you
learn every day — then this is the place for you.

The work in front of us

Some of the items on our tech roadmap for the coming year. Bets are picked a
cycle at a time and shared out, so you would take the ones that suit you and
grow into the rest.

  • Product and marketing UI in React — multi-brand, WCAG AA, strong on
    technical SEO, fast enough to hold a performance budget.
  • User management and identity — Keycloak realms, organisation hierarchies,
    partner brokering, and the entitlement model in the app.
  • API gateway work in APISIX — routes, plugins and auth policy as code.
  • Payments and billing.
  • ISO 27001 and GDPR — access control, change management, audit logging,
    observability and alerting, consent and retention.
  • The infrastructure underneath — Pulumi in TypeScript, Docker Swarm on
    Hetzner, Cloudflare at the edge, Tailscale for all engineer and CI access.
  • Third-party integrations — usually the seam between two systems that were
    never designed to meet.

Nobody arrives fluent in all of that, and we are not expecting it. We want
someone strong across a good part of it, comfortable being new to the rest, and
used to working things out — with a team and with agents, rather than alone.

Also in daily use: Postgres and PostGIS, Valkey, ClickHouse; Vite, Tailwind and
Radix; Jest and Playwright; GitHub Actions; HAProxy. Most of what we write is
TypeScript, strict — though our core API is Java and Spring, and the identity
layer has Java in it too, so how far you go into that side is up to you.

How we work

LLM-native, in the codebases you would work in. They are built around
agent-assisted development rather than merely tolerant of it — the conventions,
the tooling and the review gates all assume it. Agents do most of the
implementation and much of the review; humans design, verify and approve. What
we are really hiring for is judgement over output you did not write by hand:
knowing what to specify, what to check, and what to throw away. The bar did not
move when the tooling did.

Shape Up, and you own what you take. Roughly three weeks of building, then a
week of cooldown, with bets chosen at a betting table. We are small enough that
an area becomes yours quickly — you make the calls inside it and you answer for
how it turns out. We hand out problems, not the steps that solve them.

Remote first, with most of the team in Europe and everyone together in person at
least twice a year. Significant technical decisions get written down, and a
green build is never on its own enough to merge.

Requirements

You'll thrive here if you have…

  • Senior full-stack experience — you have owned features from the browser to
    the machine they run on.
  • A track record of taking something and running with it — a domain, a
    migration, a subsystem you took on, decided and stayed accountable for.
  • Taste. You can tell a good design from a merely plausible one, and you
    will reject work that functions but is not right — your own, and an agent's.
  • React beyond the client — server rendering, static generation, data
    loading and hydration; you know what runs where and why it matters.
  • TypeScript at strict — typed boundaries, and an instinct for when types
    are carrying real weight.
  • Infrastructure as code — Pulumi ideally; Terraform if you are ready to
    pick up Pulumi.
  • Containers and Linux in production — not writing a Dockerfile, but
    debugging a service on a machine you have to SSH into.
  • Postgres beyond queries — backup and restore, migrations, what a schema
    change does under load.
  • Wholehearted LLM-assisted development — you use coding agents daily, have
    opinions about steering them, and review their output as critically as a
    colleague's.
  • Integration instincts — third-party APIs, webhooks, OAuth/OIDC, and
    patience for other people's undocumented edge cases.
  • A working day that overlaps ours: based within CET ±3.
  • Fluent in English, our working language.

Nice to have

  • Identity and API gateways in depth — Keycloak, OIDC, SAML brokering, APISIX.
  • Compliance from the inside — an ISO 27001 certification lived through, or GDPR
    beyond a cookie banner.
  • Payment systems, billing models, or PSP integrations.
  • Observability and alerting — Prometheus, Grafana or equivalent.
  • Experience in the maritime, logistics or freight industry.
  • Familiarity with emissions accounting frameworks (GHG Protocol, GLEC, EU
    ETS..).

Benefits

As part of our team, you will:

  • 🌱 Have a chance to re-shape the future of climate in the logistics.
  • 👩‍💻 Be empowered to deliver your best work remotely, and get a stipend to set

  • 🏄‍♂️ Have a flat hierarchy, where you will have direct access to the founders
    and won't be tied up in politics.
  • 🎓 Have a high degree of learning and ownership in a dynamic environment.
  • 🏝 Take part in our team-building events.
